description: The bar chart illustrates the bias percentage across three contact conditions—“Support of Authorities,” “Extended Contact,” and “Virtual Contact”—comparing outcomes before and after exposure, segmented by prior contact type: “No Contact Before,” “Positive Contact Before,” and “Negative Contact Before,” with corresponding “After” conditions shown as stacked bars. The vertical axis represents “Bias Percentage,” ranging from 0 to 70 in increments of 10, while the horizontal axis lists the three contact conditions. For “Support of Authorities,” the “No Contact Before” bar (gray, solid) shows 39.50%, “Positive Contact Before” (pink, solid) shows 31.83%, and “Negative Contact Before” (light blue, solid) shows 42.38%; the “After” values are 0.04%, 0.00%, and 0.00% respectively, shown as small stacked segments on top. For “Extended Contact,” “No Contact Before” is 40.61%, “Positive Contact Before” is 36.13%, and “Negative Contact Before” is 47.28%; the “After” values are 0.00%, 0.00%, and 0.11%. For “Virtual Contact,” the “Before” values are 39.74% (gray, striped), 39.17% (pink, striped), and 43.83% (light blue, striped), while the “After” values are 10.00%, 10.01%, and 10.02% respectively, shown as stacked segments with diagonal hatching (gray, red, and blue). The legend clarifies that solid bars represent “Before” conditions and hatched bars represent “After” conditions, with color coding for contact type. The chart visually demonstrates a significant reduction in bias after intervention across all categories, with “Virtual Contact” showing the smallest relative reduction and the most consistent post-intervention bias levels around 10%.
